task_message:
Case V61: segment the vascular soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 161x161x177 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
The case is complete. Summary of what was done:

**Finding the lesion:** The volume is a bent extremity scanned with T2-weighted MRI. Scanning with contact sheets in all three planes, I identified a lobulated hyperintense (bright T2) soft-tissue mass within the musculature, spanning axial slices ~35–69, with a bright extension ("arm") reaching anteriorly and thin bright tails along the fascial planes.

**Segmentation steps:**
1. Started with positive points on the bright core (v1, 9.6 mL).
2. Reviewed the boundary in axial/coronal/sagittal zooms; found that the intensity-based candidate C1 (contiguous bright anterior extension) was genuine lesion tissue and accepted it (v2, 16.4 mL).
3. Checked candidate proposals C2–C5 (separate inferior/superior/anterior blobs) and judged them to be vessels/joint fluid, so rejected them.
4. Used negative points to trim a vessel leak at the superior end (v3), then re-added the missed anterior bright rim/arm with positive points (v4, 15.3 mL).
5. Verified the ends in the review and erased the residual thin fascial/vessel tails with direct mask painting above slice 69 and below slice 36 (v5, v6).

**Final:** 14.2 mL, single connected component, extent axial 35–69 / coronal 60–95 / sagittal 83–123, with the outline following the hyperintense tumor in all three planes. Confidence: medium (the anterior vascular rim boundary is the main residual uncertainty).
